acceptance_profile.description: Level 1 — Foundation. Pre-specified acceptance limits for the complete QT and QTc verification protocol.

context_of_use: Deterministic synthetic engineering QA for ECG R-peak, T-offset, QT and heart-rate-corrected QT implementations.

limitations: Synthetic signals do not establish clinical sensitivity, specificity, population generalization, or diagnostic safety.
A PASS applies only to the exact package, evidence level, verifier, algorithm build, submission, and hashes recorded in the evidence bundle.
The cited sources inform design and interpretation; none directly specifies the complete Synsigra case matrix and numeric gate set.
evidence_basis.numeric_threshold_basis: Pack-author pre-specified engineering gates selected for discrimination, regression stability, and the exact deterministic protocol; no numeric gate is copied from a cited standard or study.
evidence_basis.rationale: The protocol combines exact synthetic R-peak, T-offset, QT and formula-explicit QTc truth. Level 2 limits are engineering gates chosen for this deterministic case set; the cited guidance and studies support morphology coverage, agreement reporting, and pre-specification, not the numeric limits themselves.

sources.citation: ICH E14 Implementation Working Group. E14 Questions & Answers (R3). Last updated 10 December 2015.
sources.limitation: It explicitly states that there are no clear, widely accepted validation criteria for new automated QT methods; its clinical study guidance is not an algorithm-error threshold.
sources.relevance: Calls for independent validation of automated QT methods near the intended use, with abnormal morphology and transparent agreement analysis.
sources.title: ICH E14 Questions & Answers (R3)

sources.citation: ICH. The Clinical Evaluation of QT/QTc Interval Prolongation and Proarrhythmic Potential for Non-Antiarrhythmic Drugs. E14.
sources.limitation: The 5 ms and 10 ms values concern population-level drug-effect inference, not allowable error for an individual ECG algorithm.
sources.relevance: Provides clinical-study context for QTc correction, assay sensitivity, and drug-effect interpretation.
sources.title: ICH E14 Guideline

sources.citation: Zhou SH et al. Ann Noninvasive Electrocardiol. doi:10.1111/j.1542-474X.2009.00328.x.
sources.limitation: Its algorithm, multilead representative beats, datasets, and agreement statistics differ from Synsigra's synthetic cases.
sources.relevance: Reports automated QT agreement against CSE and an independently annotated clinical-trial database and discusses morphology and noise limitations.
sources.title: Robust QT Interval Estimation - From Algorithm to Validation

sources.citation: van Bemmel JH et al. Ann Noninvasive Electrocardiol. doi:10.1111/j.1542-474X.2009.00329.x.
sources.limitation: Reported standard deviations are study results, not universal acceptance limits for synthetic beat-level QT/QTc scoring.
sources.relevance: Provides CSE-based waveform-boundary and QT agreement context for abnormal multilead ECGs.
sources.title: Methodology of QT-Interval Measurement in the Modular ECG Analysis System (MEANS)

sources.citation: Reklewski W, Miskowicz M. Sensors. 2024;24(5):1698. doi:10.3390/s24051698.
sources.limitation: Its tested detectors, signals, noise injection, and tolerances differ from Synsigra and do not define Synsigra gate values.
sources.relevance: Shows that reported QRS performance changes with temporal tolerance, noise level, and morphology, supporting explicit multidimensional protocol disclosure.
sources.title: QRS Detector Performance Evaluation Aware of Temporal Accuracy and Presence of Noise

evidence_boundary: Synthetic engineering evidence only; not an FDA-qualified MDDT, clinical validation, diagnostic performance evidence, or a substitute for sponsor-specific protocol, risk analysis and representative clinical data.

evidence_profile.description: A permissive engineering gate for baseline implementations. It is not a clinical, regulatory, or algorithm-class claim.
evidence_profile.threshold_adjustment: Relative to Level 2: minimum gates are reduced by 0.10 (floor 0); maximum error gates are multiplied by 1.25.

truth_policy.boundary: Truncated QRS truth is not scored as an R-peak event; delineation retains its wave-specific absent and not-evaluable semantics.
truth_policy.event_scoreability: R-peak truth requires complete in-record QRS support and more than 5% retained signal during all-lead dropout; explicit exclusions are reported.
truth_policy.fiducial_limit: Model-defined endpoints do not represent human-reader uncertainty.
truth_policy.first_beat: QT is scoreable; RR-dependent QTc is excluded until a preceding in-record R peak exists.
truth_policy.qt_definition: Construction QRS onset to construction T offset.
truth_policy.qtc_definition: Scenario-declared formula applied by the cardiac timing model; formula identity is part of measurement identity.
